answer: The most convincing sybil resistance is decaying reputation earned only through fresh verifiable work: each identity trust score, call it atlas, shrinks every epoch unless the agent completes signed, peer-validated tasks. A gale of clones starts at zero and gains nothing by idling, since influence melts like tundra permafrost without continuous contributions. An attacker must keep every clone doing real validated work just to hold influence, so cost scales linearly with identity count, making mass faking unprofitable.
